correctness.rationale: Digit splitting gives exactly one mixed-parity summand pair for a mixed integer. A same-parity representation of a mixed integer must carry and thus has two positive summands. Each even-start block has 2g−1 carry-or-no-carry values; the odd-start family loses the units digit and has only g choices for the last digit because overflow is forbidden. The intersection has units zero and 2k−1 free binary digits. Removing pure outputs before inclusion–exclusion gives (3g−1)(2g−1)^(k−1)−2g^k−2^(2k−1)+1. For a positive pure integer, the number of same-parity unordered positive pairs is (∏(d_j+1)−2+I)/2, where I is 1 exactly when every active digit is even. This is one only for a lone 2 or 3 or two 1s. An opposite-parity carry gives at least two unordered pairs whenever all present digits are 1 and units is zero, because each used preceding digit has to split g, with floor(g/2)≥2 choices even at one site. A lone unit 1 has neither type. The surviving unique pure count is 5k−1 and the only missing integers are 0 and 1. Adding the two ambiguity counts gives the formula; 2g−1>4 gives the stated leading asymptotic. Independent summand enumeration reproduced all 21 recorded configurations (3,550,513 admitted pairs).
residual_risks: Finite enumeration corroborates the proof but cannot establish the all-parameter result. The exact constant is for strict complete-block cutoffs only.

originality.rationale: The distinct finding is an exact uniform exceptional-set size and exponent on natural cutoffs for g≥4. The closest published theorem gives density-one uniqueness for the very same basis; a distinct same-date ternary record gives a materially related exact formula via the same parity decomposition, but at a disjoint base with a different pure-digit correction. Neither supplies this quantified count.

The web search yielded no useful result; it and the one OEIS lookup do not rule out a differently indexed equivalent treatment. No priority direction is inferred between the two same-date records.

checked_sources: Ling & Tang's density theorem and the distinct ternary Finding
value.rationale: Density leaves the rate of exceptional representations undetermined in a classical thin additive basis. Complete two-digit blocks are natural for its parity decomposition; counting all such blocks in all higher bases gives an exact rate, coefficient and finite correction with a genuine low-base carry distinction. This is useful beyond any one verified grid and need not extend to arbitrary partitions or cutoffs to be worthwhile.
residual_risks: The absence of 0 and 1 representations and the underlying thin-basis properties alone are not the contribution.
